On this page

Peer agents ​

A peer connection lets one agent ask an independent specialist for help. The specialist keeps its own instructions, tools, and sessions. On Cursor hosting, team-owned agents reach each other by deployment slug, and Agent SDK handles routing and authentication for you.

Delegate a question to a specialist ​

Ask the concierge about the weather, and it hands the question to the weather agent and returns the answer.

ts
// bot/mcp-connections/weather.ts
import { defineConnection } from "@grok/agent-sdk/connections";

export default defineConnection({
  agent: "weather-agent",
  description: "Delegate weather questions to the weather specialist.",
});

The filename, weather.ts, becomes the MCP server name, and agent is the specialist's lowercase deployment slug. Give the concierge a one-way routing rule, so the agents never pass a request back and forth:

md
When a request needs current weather, ask the `weather` peer. Return its
answer.

Deploy both agents from pushed Git refs:

bash
agent-sdk deploy --dir ./agents/weather-agent --slug weather-agent
agent-sdk deploy --dir ./agents/concierge --slug concierge

Continue the specialist's session ​

The first ask returns { status, sessionId, reply } as text. Pass that sessionId on the next ask to continue the specialist's earlier work.

ts
const first = await ctx.host.mcp.callTool("weather", "ask", {
  message: "What's the weather in Paris right now?",
});
const firstText = first.content.find((part) => part.type === "text");
if (firstText?.text === undefined) {
  throw new Error("weather ask returned no text payload");
}
const { sessionId } = JSON.parse(firstText.text) as { sessionId: string };

await ctx.host.mcp.callTool("weather", "ask", {
  message: "How does that compare with tomorrow?",
  sessionId,
});

If the specialist is still working, ask returns status: "running", and check waits for the answer.

ts
await ctx.host.mcp.callTool("weather", "check", {
  sessionId,
  waitSeconds: 20,
});

Call a peer tool directly ​

Use call_tool when you want to run a tool on a peer agent directly, without starting a model turn on that agent. The peer needs at least one server tool, and the call follows the direct-call rules.

ts
const result = await ctx.host.mcp.callTool("weather", "call_tool", {
  toolName: "get_forecast",
  input: { city: "Paris" },
});
const part = result.content.find((item) => item.type === "text");
if (part?.text === undefined) {
  return { ok: false, forecast: null };
}
const payload = JSON.parse(part.text) as {
  isError?: boolean;
  result?: unknown;
};

return {
  ok: result.isError !== true && payload.isError !== true,
  forecast: payload.result ?? null,
};

Try it locally ​

To try it locally, run both projects in one process:

bash
agent-sdk dev ./agents
agent-sdk chat --url http://127.0.0.1:3000/concierge \
  --message "What's the weather in Paris right now?"

Locally, agent is the specialist's mount slug, usually its directory name.

Peer or subagent? ​

Use a subagent to split one agent's job into roles. Use a peer when the specialist is a complete agent you also run on its own.

SubagentPeer
ContextChild role inside one agentIndependent agent and session
Tools and connectionsInherits the parent projectOwns its project surface
ReachabilityParent onlyLocal co-hosted agents, or declared deployments on the same team

Other hosts ​

To self-host, run the peers under one agent-sdk process, and if turns run on remote workers, protect it with --bearer-token and set --public-url as Deployment describes.
